# Open choices: product-defaults

`aidd-team:product-defaults` leaves these decisions to the team. aidd's default holds until a `standards` entry fills one. `aidd standard list` names the library standards for each choice, and `aidd standard add` adopts one.

| Choice | Question | aidd's default | Options |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication` | What signs people in and keeps their sessions? | The web framework's own sign-in where it has one, such as Django's, Spring Security, or ASP.NET Core Identity. Else, or once several apps share sign-in or a customer needs SSO, a self-hosted OpenID Connect provider: Keycloak. Never a hand-rolled flow. | the framework's own, Keycloak, ZITADEL, Ory, authentik, Auth0, Amazon Cognito, Microsoft Entra External ID |
| `access-control` | Where are the permission rules kept and checked? | In the application's code: roles and permissions in one policy module, built from the authorization matrix, that every path and object asks. A policy engine, OpenFGA, once access follows relationships such as sharing or nested teams, or several services share the rules. | roles in the application's code, OpenFGA, Cedar, Open Policy Agent, SpiceDB, Casbin |
| `email-provider` | Which service sends the product's transactional email? | The email service of the host the project already runs, such as Amazon SES on AWS, behind one mail module. A dedicated transactional email provider where the host has none. | Amazon SES, Postmark, SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, the company's SMTP relay |
